findings.statement: The parameter-free upstream-speed transit scale outperforms the orientation correction in every reserved configuration.
findings.applicability: Configuration→particle category→trajectory averaging; 76 reserved trajectories across 3 configurations; upstream-only native windows.
findings.limitations: Two-dimensional orientation, ambiguous thickness/fluid metadata and absent normal stress block a unique drag mechanism. Constant-speed success does not prove unchanged drag.
falsification: Require every predictor row strictly before interface entry; prohibit interpolation across entry.
Reproduce nested configuration→particle weighting on every covered subset.
Keep duplicate trajectory representations linked and do not infer thickness or unmeasured normal stress.
findings.prior_art: Ballistic transit is established; preserved falsification is the contribution rather than an admitted new settling law. This review uses retained prior-art records only; it performs no new literature priority adjudication.
